keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Candia row; Crete is drawn inside nobody's shape between the Emirate of Crete's end in 960 and the Ottoman conquest). The whole island: 'Venetian troops first occupied the island in 1205' and it was 'secured' only in 1212; from 1206 the Genoese Enrico Pescatore held 'large parts' (Pescatore page), so the ledger's contest_start 1206 / contest_end 1217 covers 1206-1216. No area on the page (the island is about 8,300 km2 today).

correction.text: Candia (Chandax, modern Heraklion) and its walls and hinterland

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Venice's remnant. The Siege of Candia page: after Canea (1645) and Rethymno (1646) the Ottomans held 'near-total possession of the island', leaving Candia and 'half a dozen small isolated castles' (Souda, Spinalonga, Gramvousa) in Venetian hands. The shape is Candia and its hinterland at a 25 km radius, an upper bound.

ledger.note: 1205: Venetian troops occupy Crete. The page: Venice acquired the island from Boniface of Montferrat on 12 August 1204 for silver marks and an annual revenue share; 'Venetian troops first occupied the island in 1205' and the island was 'secured' only in 1212. The 10 September 1211 charter (Carta Concessionis) and the 20 March 1212 first colonist wave mark the settlement.

1206: the Genoese Enrico Pescatore, Count of Malta, seizes Crete. 'From 1206, Pescatore took control of large parts of Crete.' The Kingdom of Candia page adds that Venice's attack of summer 1207 failed, that Venice took Palaiokastro near Candia in 1209 and that Pescatore was evicted by 1212; the Pescatore page says the Genoese 'held onto Chania'. The pages name no regions.

1217: Genoa gives up Crete. 'A treaty ended the war with Genoa' on 11 May 1217, 'leaving Crete in Venetian hands'. Pescatore himself was out by 1212; Chania stayed Genoese until the treaty on the Pescatore page's reading, which neither page dates.

region.text: Candia, where the Venetian feudal lords rose against new harbour taxes and declared a 'Republic of Saint Titus'

ledger.note: 1363: Venetian colonists rebel at Candia. The page: on 9 August 1363 the feudal lords rose against new harbour taxes and the rebels declared a 'Republic of Saint Titus'; it names Candia but not how far the rebellion reached.

1364: Venice crushes the rebels. 'A Venetian fleet arrived on 7 May, and Candia surrendered on 9 May.' The major Cretan revolts ended in April 1367 when the Kallergis brothers were captured by treason.

region.text: Canea (Chania), which fell after a siege of 56 days

ledger.note: 1645: Canea falls. The Ottoman fleet arrived off Crete on 23 June 1645 and landed about 15 miles west of Canea; 'The city fell on 22 August 1645, after a siege that lasted for 56 days.'

region.text: Rethymno, its citadel holding out to 13 November 1646

ledger.note: 1646: Rethymno falls. 'The city fell on 20 October 1646, and its citadel held out until 13 November 1646' (Cretan War page); the Siege of Candia page gives 13 November.

ledger.note: 1648: the island is Ottoman except Candia. The Cretan War page: 'The eastern half of the island was conquered in 1647, except for the fortress of Siteia', and 'By the beginning of 1648, all of Crete, except Candia and a few strongholds like the island of Gramvousa, was in Ottoman hands.' Confidence 2: the districts fell during 1646-1647 and the event is placed at the start of 1648, where the next shape begins. (Reviewer eu-05-x, 2026-10-19: source changed from the Siege of Candia page and confidence raised from 1 after reading the Cretan War page.)

ledger.note: 1648: the Ottomans besiege Candia. 'The siege began in May 1648'; the 21-year siege is the longest in the history of the war; Venice counter-attacked elsewhere (the Aegean, Dalmatia, Lemnos and Tenedos in 1655-56) to relieve it.

region.text: Candia (Chandax, modern Heraklion) and its walls and hinterland

ledger.note: 1669: Candia surrenders. 'On 5 September 1669, the city was surrendered to the Ottomans' (the Siege of Candia infobox gives 27 September); about 3,754 soldiers and 4,000 civilians left; Venice kept the three island forts and Tinos and Kythera.

region.text: Candia (Chandax, modern Heraklion) and its walls and hinterland

ledger.note: 1669: Venice loses Candia, and Crete with it. The surrender 'sealed the fate of the island and ended the war in an Ottoman victory'.

ledger.note: 1669: the Kingdom of Candia ends after 464 years. Infobox 'Dissolution: 1669'. Spinalonga, Gramvousa and Souda, which Venice kept, fall to the Ottomans in 1715.

wars.name: Genoese-Venetian war for Crete
wars.outcome: Enrico Pescatore took large parts of Crete from 1206; Venice failed in 1207, took Palaiokastro in 1209 and drove him out by 1212; a treaty of 11 May 1217 ended the war with Crete in Venetian hands.
wars.note: Pescatore page: 'From 1206, Pescatore took control of large parts of Crete'; the Genoese 'held onto Chania'; Alamanno da Costa began a campaign in 1211. The page names no regions.

wars.name: Revolt of Skordyles and Melissenos
wars.outcome: The Cretan rebels reached a treaty with Venice on 13 September 1219.
wars.note: Hagiostephanites's revolt on the Lasithi plateau (1212) is the page's earlier rising.

wars.name: Revolt of Alexios Kallergis
wars.outcome: The largest revolt to that date began in 1282 and ended with the Peace of Alexios Kallergis, signed on 28 April 1299.
wars.note: The page names no regions held by the rebels; the Alexios Kallergis article did not load.

wars.name: Revolt of Saint Titus
wars.outcome: The Venetian feudal lords rose on 9 August 1363 and declared the Republic of Saint Titus; a Venetian fleet arrived on 7 May 1364 and Candia surrendered on 9 May. The Kallergis brothers were captured in April 1367, ending the major revolts.

wars.name: Cretan War
wars.outcome: The Ottomans landed on 23 June 1645, took Canea (22 August 1645) and Rethymno (20 October 1646), held near-total possession of the island by 1648 and besieged Candia from May 1648 until it surrendered on 5 September 1669.
wars.note: The Siege of Candia page gives the surrender's end date as 27 September 1669. Venice kept Spinalonga, Gramvousa, Souda, Tinos and Kythera and tripled its Dalmatian holdings.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border. The 1206-1217 Genoese holdings and the Cretan revolts are the exceptions (soft).
The Ottoman-Venetian front in the Cretan War is not described district by district on any page opened; the fortress of Candia and the three island forts are points, not lines.
